newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.S. soldier in Germany gets five years for rape.
newsitem.headline: U.S. soldier in Germany gets five years for rape.

text.p: A U.S. military court sentenced an army sergeant on Thursday to five years in jail after finding him guilty of raping and forcibly sodomising female soldiers at an army base in Germany.

Sergeant First Class Paul Fuller, 25, of Columbus, Ohio, described by his defence lawyer as "something of a playboy", showed no emotion when a jury member read the verdict in the latest case of sex abuse to taint the American armed forces.

Prosecutors had sought a life prison term for Fuller after a jury convicted him of one count of rape and three counts of sodomy involving three female soldiers as well as three counts of cruelty and one count of kidnapping.

They called Fuller a "sexual predator" who took advantage of his rank to get sexual gratification. "This is a man who treated his barracks as his own kingdom and had a harem at his disposal," Army prosecutor Captain Chris Hellmich said.

Defence lawyers argued that race had played a major role in bringing the charges against Fuller, who is black, and said he was the victim of a prejudiced investigation that turned into a witchhunt by overzealous prosecutors.

Fuller stopped short of admitting the charges but apologised for his behaviour toward his victims, who were present in the court room. He asked the court for leniency and said he was sorry to have dishonoured his deceased father, an army veteran.

"I have failed to uphold the standards of the army," said Fuller, speaking so quietly he had to be asked twice by the judge to speak louder. "I joined the army to follow my father's footsteps. I'm sorry dad."
Two women who had testified against Fuller, a mechanic, told the court after the verdict that he should be given a short jail term. Fuller had spent two months in jail while awaiting trial.
One said she did not feel she was a victim until told so by criminal investigators.
"It upsets me because I do not feel as though I am a victim," said Private Melissa Mitchell. "He has already served some time in prison and that should be enough."

But another woman told the court she would probably never recover. "I felt alone, very scared with him. The emotional pain was more than the physical pain," said Private Shelly Marshall. "It has changed the way I look at people."

Fuller is the second sergeant to be convicted at this army base 30 km (19 miles) south of Frankfurt on sex abuse charges involving newly-arrived soldiers who attended a two-week orientation programme before joining their units in Germany.

Another soldier at the base, Sergeant First Class Julius Davis, 37, of Fayetteville, North Carolina, was acquitted last week of rape and sodomy but given two years jail after being found guilty of lesser charges, including indecent assault.

Fuller's laywer, U.S. Army Major Peter Becker, told jurors in closing arguments on Wednesday that female soldiers testifying against Fuller had "cried fake tears" and were coached to appear as victims in court in a racially-motivated investigation.
"The investigators told these women, who had engaged in consensual sex, 'Are you going to be a victim or a slut?' It is a horrible situation," Becker said.
"Anybody who says that race is not an issue in this trial is wrong," he said.

Fuller was also found guilty of one count each of unlawfully entering a soldier's room, fraternisation with a lower-ranking soldier and indecent assault. He was acquitted of one count of attempted rape and obstruction of justice.
